description: Strict Candidate Eligibility Gate. Phase 12 update (2026-09-21): Cross-scene validation COMPLETED via frozen snapshot timing on bicycle and garden (real cameras). M1 tile32: FOUND SCENE-DEPENDENT — room +58%, outdoor -44%. M3 SH degree: cross-scene quality consistent, but NOT a performance knob (<4% timing impact). No module qualifies as universal performance candidate. Composability: NOT RECOMMENDED.

forward_correctness.description: Forward pixel equivalence verified (bit-exact or max_pixel_error < 0.01)

training_sanity.description: 500-step pass with real GT, no NaN/Inf, loss decreasing

M1_tile16.name: tile_size=16 (default)
M1_tile16.note: Default configuration; full room training complete with tile16

M1_tile32.name: tile_size=32
M1_tile32.note: Room 30K: 1.58× faster, PSNR+0.12dB, NaN-free. Phase 12 cross-scene (bicycle/garden, frozen snapshot, real camera): tile32 is SLOWER (0.69×). Scene-dependent: +58% indoor (1.6M Gs), -44% outdoor (5.8-6.1M Gs). 30K training on bicycle/garden LOCALLY_INFEASIBLE (peak 8.27GB on 8GB GPU). tile32 is NOT universally beneficial.

scene_dependence.conclusion: Scene-dependent. Optimal tile size depends on scene and hardware.

M2.name: packed/dense
M2.note: Phase 10A (2026-09-23, local RTX 5070): Full 30K training COMPLETED for both packed and dense modes on room. Packed: 62.2min, 31.36dB. Dense: 64.3min, 31.29dB. BOTH STABLE — zero NaN/Inf. Nearly identical Gaussian trajectory (0.07% final diff). Identical VRAM (2,911MB). Key finding: M2 packed/dense is functionally a NO-OP for single-camera training — no meaningful performance, quality, or trajectory difference. The packed inference advantage (2.02x) does not translate to training. All gates PASS → eligible_for_composability=true.

M3.name: SH degree (0/1/3)
M3.note: Phase 9C (2026-08-23, local RTX 5070): Full 30K training COMPLETED for SH0/SH1/SH3 on room. ALL STABLE — zero NaN/Inf. SH0: 38.1min, 32.34dB best PSNR, 1,041MB VRAM. SH1: 42.8min, 32.22dB, 1,398MB VRAM. SH3: 68.7min, ~31.44dB, 2,824MB VRAM. Gaussian trajectory nearly identical across degrees. Dominant cost: optimizer (scales with SH param count). All gates PASS → eligible_for_composability=true. Cross-scene (bicycle, garden) still PENDING. See reports/epic05/phase9c_m3_full_training.md.

M4.name: radius_clip
M4.note: Phase 11 (2026-09-21, local RTX 5070): Forward+Gradient+GT Quality all PASS. Workload analysis shows <1% intersection reduction at quality-preserving thresholds. FALSIFIED for E2E benefit.

M5.name: eps2d
M5.note: Phase 11 (2026-09-21, local RTX 5070): Forward+Gradient+GT Quality all PASS. Default eps2d=0.3 is at quality optimum. FALSIFIED for E2E benefit.

M6.name: HiGS inference renderer
M6.note: Inference-only renderer — no backward pass. Cannot participate in training. Removed from Phase 8 scope.

M7.name: HiGS SH compression
M7.note: Inference-only. SH32 quality OK (64.85 dB min), SH16 degraded (49.79 dB min). Removed from Phase 8 scope.

M9.name: TC-GS (Tensor Core)
M9.note: External repository. Removed from Phase 8 gsplat optimization scope.

M2.effort_to_qualify: COMPLETED Phase 10A (2026-09-23, local RTX 5070): Full 30K training for both packed and dense modes completed. All gates PASS. M2 now eligible_for_composability=true. Functionally a NO-OP for training performance.

M3.effort_to_qualify: COMPLETED Phase 9C (2026-08-23, local RTX 5070): Full 30K training for SH0/SH1/SH3 completed. All gates PASS. M3 now eligible_for_composability=true.

M4.effort_to_qualify: EVALUATED Phase 11 (2026-09-21): Forward/Gradient/GT Quality all PASS. However, workload analysis shows radius_clip provides <1% intersection reduction at quality-preserving thresholds. Training would not improve on this. Marked FALSIFIED for performance benefit.

M5.effort_to_qualify: EVALUATED Phase 11 (2026-09-21): Forward/Gradient/GT Quality all PASS. Default eps2d=0.3 confirmed as quality optimum. Reducing eps2d costs up to 1.61dB PSNR. No quality-preserving configuration change possible. Marked FALSIFIED for performance benefit.

phase13a_oracle.key_finding: tpg_std (tiles_per_gauss standard deviation) predicts tile-size winner with 93.3% accuracy. Threshold: tpg_std > 135 → tile32. p95_intersections_per_tile (effect_size=3.06), tpg_mean (effect_size=3.50) also strong predictors. Synthetic camera is fundamentally misleading — real camera MUST be used.
phase13a_oracle.recommendation: Scene-level static oracle is sufficient (room always tile32 after early training, outdoor always tile16). Adaptive kernel NOT yet justified — need training-level validation.
phase13a_oracle.next_step: Phase 13B: Validate oracle on real training data (fwd+bwd over actual training trajectory)

blocker.details: Cross-scene validated via frozen snapshot (bicycle/garden real cameras). 30K training locally infeasible (OOM). tile32 scene-dependent: +58% room, -44% outdoor. No Tier A universal candidate.
blocker.impact: No module qualifies as universal performance candidate. Composability not recommended.

phase13A_predictor_revision.reason: Threshold-based binary predictor does not generalize to multi-tile space

M1_tile_size_expanded.decoupling_finding: RENDERER/TRAINING DECOUPLING CONFIRMED — room forward-snapshot-optimal (tile20) ≠ fwd+bwd-optimal (tile16) ≠ 30K-training-optimal (tile32). Snapshot winner does NOT predict training winner.
M1_tile_size_expanded.phase13A_predictor_revision: FRAGILE. Binary threshold does not generalize to 8-tile space. Simple ranking rules (tpg_std ranking) are monotonic but insufficient for exact prediction.

phase14A_tile20_anomaly.root_cause: Asynchronous topology spillover on densification iterations

phase14B_sorting.segmented_sort_reason: 1.9-4.5x slower than global radix sort in all tile/config combinations. Pixel correct (bit-exact).

phase15_implementation_recon.method: Full CUDA source audit of gsplat rasterization pipeline: IntersectTile.cu, ProjectionEWA3DGS*.cu, RasterizeToPixels3DGS*.cu, SphericalHarmonicsCUDA.cu, Intersect.cpp, Common.h, Rasterization.h, Intersect.h.
phase15_implementation_recon.forward_bottleneck: Intersection generation + global radix sort pipeline (S3→S5). n_isects up to 176M. Sort covers 45-bit key, ~12 CUB passes, 24×n_isects bytes memory traffic.
phase15_implementation_recon.backward_bottleneck: Backward kernel re-reads all forward input tensors from global memory (~10 tensor reads) + gpuAtomicAdd contention for gradient writes.
phase15_implementation_recon.largest_data_structure: isect_ids / flatten_ids at n_isects elements. For tile16: ~1.4GB + 700MB + sorted variants + CUB temp ~3GB = ~6-7GB total.

candidate_C1_depth_compression.description: Reduce sort key depth field from 32-bit to 16-bit (upper half of float32). Sort passes: 12→8 (33% reduction). ~10 lines in 1 file. Zero backward/gradient risk.

candidate_C2_sync_elimination.description: Replace .item<int64_t>() host sync in Intersect.cpp with pre-allocated max-size buffers and GPU-side n_isects tracking. Eliminates 5-30μs sync per iteration.

candidate_C4_atomic_reduction.description: Shared-memory gradient accumulator in backward kernel. Merges 8 warps→1 atomicAdd per gaussian per tile. 8× fewer atomic calls.

candidate_C3_buffer_reuse.description: Pre-allocate intersection buffers at max capacity. Modest benefit given PyTorch caching allocator.

candidate_C5_float16_storage.description: Float16 storage for fwd colors/opacities. Standard technique, modest benefit.

phase15_implementation_recon.no_high_confidence_status: If C1 fails forward-only ablation, conclusion becomes NO HIGH-CONFIDENCE CANDIDATE — renderer near performance frontier for current algorithm.
phase15_implementation_recon.next_phase_recommendation: A — implement C1 (depth bit-width compression) as independent ablation

phase16_C1_implementation.verdict: C1 is CORRECT but NOT BENEFICIAL
phase16_C1_implementation.verdict_type: D (Sort not faster on this GPU)

key_encoding_verified.depth_encoding: IEEE 754 float32 bitcast→uint32, zero-extended. NO quantization.

phase16_C1_implementation.ordering_correctness: ZERO inversions (mathematically proven). Ties within <0.8% depth.
phase16_C1_implementation.conclusion: 33% fewer sort passes exists theoretically but does not produce measurable forward speedup. CUB radix sort is not the forward bottleneck — rasterization dominates.

phase17B_C17_1_tile_local_queues.verdict: CORRECT (feasibility proven) — CUDA implementation required for speed measurement

memory_analysis.two_pass_mitigation: drops to ~59 MB with per-tile exact allocation

phase17B_C17_1_tile_local_queues.comparison_with_phase14B: C17-1 is architecturally different from Phase 14B segmented sort. Phase 14B (1.9-4.5× slower) re-sorted already-materialized global arrays. C17-1 avoids global materialization from inception — direct per-tile writes + block-level local sort.
phase17B_C17_1_tile_local_queues.relationship_with_C1: C1 depth compression was pre-applied to the installed gsplat. Phase 17B restored the TRUE baseline (v1.5.3, full 32-bit depth sort) for all validation. Key takeaway: C17-1 sorting by full float32 depth would be MORE correct than C1's 16-bit depth_upper sort.
phase17B_C17_1_tile_local_queues.next_step: Phase 17C: C17-2 Two-Phase Sort (simpler CUDA implementation, fewer file changes). C17-1 CUDA implementation deferred pending C17-2 results.
